skill.name: react-modernization
skill.description: Modernize React applications by planning version upgrades, converting class components to hooks, applying codemods, and adopting React 18 patterns.
skill.summary: Guides React upgrades, hooks migration, React 18 adoption, codemods, TypeScript, and performance modernization.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown-only React modernization guide. Most static findings are false positives from code fences, local lazy imports, relative fetch examples, and variable names. One medium risk remains because the codemod section recommends global npm installation and unpinned npx package execution.

remediation.suggestion: Replace global npm installs and unpinned npx commands with pinned devDependencies or pinned package versions, and require review before codemods change files.

content.value_statement: Legacy React apps become harder to upgrade when class patterns, older render APIs, and manual migrations accumulate. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for hooks, React 18 features, codemods, TypeScript, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains React 16 to 18 breaking changes and upgrade sequencing.
Maps class state, lifecycle methods, context, and HOCs to hooks.
Shows React 18 root API, batching, transitions, and Suspense examples.
Lists codemod commands for JSX transform and unsafe lifecycle migration.
Provides a migration checklist for testing, performance, and rollout.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts in the published file.
Codemod examples require review before running on production code.
Does not cover React 19 features or framework-specific migrations.
Referenced supplemental files are listed but not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a Legacy App
use_cases.description: Plan a React 16 or 17 upgrade with clear sequencing, testing steps, and React 18 adoption notes.

use_cases.title: Convert Classes to Hooks
use_cases.description: Translate class state, lifecycle methods, context consumers, and higher-order components into functional patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Migration Workflows
use_cases.description: Create team guidance for codemods, TypeScript typing, performance checks, and migration checklists.

prompt_templates.title: Find Migration Targets
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of an existing app
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my React app structure and identify components that should move from class syntax to hooks. Produce a staged migration checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Plan React 18 Upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me upgrade this React 17 app to React 18. Focus on createRoot, StrictMode warnings, automatic batching, and test updates.

prompt_templates.title: Design Codemod Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a codemod plan for replacing unsafe lifecycles and applying the new JSX transform. Include verification steps before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize at Scale
prompt_templates.prompt: Modernize this large React codebase with TypeScript, Suspense, transitions, and performance measurements. Prioritize changes by risk and impact.

output_examples.input: I have a React 16 app with many class components and limited tests.
output: A phased upgrade plan from React 16 to React 17, then React 18.
A component inventory that separates safe hook conversions from risky shared components.
A testing checklist for lifecycle behavior, StrictMode warnings, and regression coverage.

output_examples.input: My team wants to replace unsafe lifecycle methods and adopt the new JSX transform.
output: A codemod rollout plan with package version review and branch isolation.
A verification checklist for diffs, tests, lint results, and manual review.
Guidance for communicating migration rules to other frontend contributors.

output_examples.input: We want to add React 18 transitions without hurting input responsiveness.
output: A recommendation for separating urgent input state from deferred result updates.
A review list for loading states, Suspense boundaries, and user-visible latency.
Performance checks to compare render frequency before and after the change.

best_practices: Upgrade incrementally and keep each migration step small enough to review.
Run tests and inspect warnings after each React version or codemod change.
Pin codemod tooling versions and review generated diffs before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not migrate every component at once without a rollback plan.
Do not add useMemo or useCallback without a measured performance reason.
Do not ignore StrictMode warnings during React 18 validation.

faq.question: Can this skill update code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and examples, but the published package contains only a Markdown skill file.

faq.question: Does it support React 18?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers createRoot, automatic batching, transitions, Suspense, and StrictMode migration concerns.

faq.question: Can it help convert class components to hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps state, lifecycle methods, context, HOCs, and custom hooks into modern functional patterns.

faq.question: Are codemods safe to run without review?
faq.answer: No. Pin tool versions, run them on a branch, and review all generated changes before merging.

faq.question: Does it include TypeScript migration advice?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for component props, ReactNode children, and generic component typing.

faq.question: Does it cover framework migrations such as Next.js?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on React application patterns, not framework-specific routing or server features.
